texts.facts: This DAR was filed on 06.08.2024 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties. The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 28.05.2024 in which one Smt. Malti Devi W/o Late Sh. Chatri Bind (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries. As per petitioner, on 28.05.2024, she was going to Naya Bazar, Delhi for selling the pulses etc. at about 06.00 A.M., a vehicle bearing no. DL-1LAC-2671 (TATA LGV) (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") which was driven by its driver (herein R-1) came from S.N. Marg, Lahori Gate, Delhi-110006, in a very rash, negligent and careless manner and without blowing any horn or apply safety measures, hit her and due to this heavy impact, she fell down on the road and received injuries on her left foot. She and her daughter went to Sushruta Trauma Centre, Civil Lines, Delhi in TSR of R-1 where her MLC bearing no. 1768/2024 dated 28.05.2024 was prepared by the doctors and thereafter, she took treatment at Raksha Deep Ortho Research Centre, Lal Kothi, Bari Bazar, Munger-811201. An FIR no. 299/2024, U/s 279/337 IPC, PS Lahori Gate was registered by the police with respect to above accident. R-1 is stated to be the driver, R-2 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle. R-3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Malti Devi (I)(Fir299/2024/Lahori ... vs Daya Ram (Sbi Gen. Ins0 on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171359874/ 3 DAR was treated as a claim petition. R-3/insurance company Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2025.07.14 16:01:41 +0530 was directed to file a legal offer/reasoned decision in response to the said DAR. R-1 and R-2 were also directed to file their Written Statements. 2. However, no written statement was filed either by R-1 or R-2. R-3/Insurance Company filed a legal offer which was not accepted by the petitioner. ISSUES 3. EVIDENCE 4. In support of the claim, petitioner examined herself in her evidence and filed affidavit Ex. PW1/A wherein she described the occurrence of incident in line with the facts mentioned in Para no.1 of this award. She further stated that she was selling the pulses, dry fruits etc. on patri at Mithaipul, PANKAJ Date: SHARMA 2025.07.14 16:01:44 +0530 Near Peeli Kothi, Naya Bazar, Delhi-110006 and earning about Rs.25,000/- per month. She was about 57 years of age at the time of accident. She spent Rs.50,000/- on her medical treatment, Rs.40,000/- on conveyance, Rs.40,000/- on special diet and Rs.50,000/- on attendant charges. She stated that she is entitled to get compensation of Rs.40,00,000/-. She has relied upon the following documents viz:- "Complete set of DAR Ex. PW-1/1(colly); Discharge summary Ex. PW-1/2; Treatment papers Ex. PW-1/3(colly); Her medical bills Ex. PW-1/4(colly); Her disability certificate Ex. PW-1/5; and Copy of her Aadhaar Card Ex. PW-1/6." 4.1 She was cross- examined by Ld. Counsel for R-3/ Insurance Company. In her cross-examination, she deposed that she has not filed any education proof, employment proof or earning proof on record. She deposed that she has no document to show amounts as mentioned in para no.9 of her Malti Devi (I)(Fir299/2024/Lahori ... vs Daya Ram (Sbi Gen. Ins0 on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171359874/ 4 affidavit except Ex. PW-1/4. She deposed that though she is taking medicines, however, no medical prescription is there. She deposed that presently she is not doing anything. 4.2 PE was then closed. Respondents have not led any evidence in respondent's evidence and therefore, RE was closed. ARGUMENTS AND FINDINGS The amount of FDRs on maturity would be released in her savings/MACT Claims SB Account as and when she furnishes the details of her bank account which is near the place of her residence to the Bank Manager, State Bank of India, Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi under intimation to this Tribunal. 25.2 The Bank(s) shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the petitioner(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the petitioner(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2025.07.14 16:02:22 +0530 not a joint account(s). However, the statement containing FDR number, FDR amount, date of maturity and maturity amount shall be furnished by the bank to the petitioner(s).
texts.arguments: Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310. Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Digitally signed by PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2025.07.14 16:02:06 +0530 Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343. 17. Accordingly, the aforementioned disability certificate could be read in evidence in terms of the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Union of India in Writ Petition (s) (Civil ) No (s). 534/2020 date of order 16/11/2021. Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,(2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a recent judgment dated 31.10.2017 given in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, the multiplier of '5' is held applicable for calculating the loss of future earnings of petitioner arising out of her above disability.
